title: Save often
body: The 3DS version lets you save from the pause menu almost anywhere — you don’t need to find a save point like in the original N64 release.

title: Listen to Navi
body: When Navi flashes yellow over an object or enemy, target it with C-up: there’s almost always a hint, a key item, or a boss weakness behind it.

title: Get the Stone of Agony as early as you can
body: It’s the 20-Gold-Skulltula reward and rumbles near secrets — bomb-able cracks, hidden switches, soft soil. Start hunting Skulltulas from Kokiri Forest onward.

title: Keep a fairy bottled
body: Catch at least one fairy from a hollow tree or Great Fairy fountain before a hard dungeon — it’s a free automatic revive.

title: Control the clock with your ocarina
body: The Sun’s Song instantly flips day and night — use it to skip waiting around, scare off ReDeads, or catch a shop only open at a certain time.

title: Swap shields before fire
body: The Deku Shield burns up in lava and fire attacks. Switch to the Hylian Shield (or the Mirror Shield, as adult) before Death Mountain and the Fire Temple.

title: Start the trading sequence early
body: Several items in the chain toward Biggoron’s Sword spoil within minutes or in-game hours. Check the Sidequests page as soon as you have the adult Ocarina and plan your route.

title: Never run out of Bombchus
body: Buy them at Bombchu Bowling (Castle Town) and from the night-time traveling merchant in Kokiri Forest — they’re the only way to hit certain distant switches and eyes.
